assertion: It's an unusually quiet conclusion to a season that defied expectations and broke a 121-year-old hurricane record.
inaccuracy: The article says Isaias broke the 121-year-old record; the evidence says Isaias reaching hurricane status on Oct 8 only tied the 1905 season for the latest first hurricane.
independent_value: Wikipedia 2026 season: Isaias tied the 1905 season for latest first hurricane.

assertion: The hurricane drought ended Oct. 8, when Isaias became the Atlantic's first hurricane of the season, breaking a 121-year record for the latest first hurricane.
inaccuracy: The article says Isaias broke the record; the evidence says it tied 1905 (an outright record only for the satellite era).

assertion: 10 named storms, the fewest since 2014, when there were only eight storms.
It was also the first time since 1925 that there was only one hurricane in the entire season.
reason: 1925 did have 1 hurricane per the season list, but I could not verify that no season between 1925 and 2026 had exactly one; no warehouse table carries HURDAT.
measure: number of hurricanes per Atlantic season historical
searched: Atlantic hurricane seasons with one hurricane since 1925

assertion: The first record fell in September when the Atlantic went without a hurricane through Sept. 21, breaking a 112-year record.
independent_value: Wikipedia: first season since 1914 with no hurricane this late, third since 1851.

assertion: Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, at 8:30 p.m. CDT Friday, Oct. 9, as a Category 2 hurricane, peaking as a Category 3 with 120 mph winds.
independent_value: Wikipedia Isaias: landfall 01:30 UTC Oct 10 (8:30 pm CDT Oct 9) near Destin as Cat 2; peak 120 mph Cat 3.

assertion: Isaias contributed to more than 20 tornadoes, and as many as eight people were killed by indirect storm impacts.
independent_value: 24 tornadoes confirmed; 9 total fatalities (6 FL, 2 AL, 1 SC), consistent with up to eight indirect.

assertion: AccuWeather preliminarily estimated $16 to $20 billion in total damage and economic loss from Isaias.
reason: Preliminary AccuWeather estimate, correctly attributed. Context omitted: Wikipedia lists at least $2 billion in damage.

assertion: AccuWeather estimated $4 to $6 billion in total damage and economic loss from Arthur.
reason: The AccuWeather Arthur page returned HTTP 403 so the estimate could not be read; Wikipedia cites lower estimates (Gallagher US$1.3 billion; its table lists $700 million), so the figure is not corroborated.
why_not: The '$4' match on the Wikipedia page is 'US$400 million', a Gallagher estimate for Bertha, not an Arthur or AccuWeather figure, so it does not change the grade.
measure: Atlantic hurricane named storms HURDAT tropical cyclone
searched: AccuWeather Arthur total damage and economic loss estimate
why_no_page: AccuWeather page 403; no other page located.

assertion: The season opened in mid-June when Tropical Storm Arthur made landfall near Matagorda Bay, Texas, and set off flooding across the Gulf Coast.
inaccuracy: The article says landfall near Matagorda Bay; Wikipedia says landfall near Galveston, Texas.
warehouse_value: FEMA DR-4927-LA (2026-06-30) and DR-4930-MS (2026-08-03), TROPICAL STORM ARTHUR
sql: SELECT declaration_title, fema_declaration_string, declaration_date, COUNT(*) n FROM disasters.disaster_declarations WHERE "year" = 2026 AND (declaration_title LIKE '%ARTHUR%' OR declaration_title LIKE '%LALA%' OR declaration_title LIKE '%NOLO%') GROUP BY declaration_title, fema_declaration_string, declaration_date
independent_value: Wikipedia: Arthur formed June 17, landfall near Galveston; flooding along Gulf Coast.
why_not: The Gallagher loss figures on the Wikipedia page are dollar estimates, not the landfall location and flooding graded here.

assertion: The same El Nino that muzzled the Atlantic supercharged the eastern Pacific; as of Nov. 3 the central and eastern Pacific had produced 24 named storms, including 13 hurricanes, and Vance became the basin's 11th major hurricane.
independent_value: Wikipedia Pacific season: 13 hurricanes, 11 majors (record tied with 2015); 25 storms now, consistent with 24 as of Nov 3. El Nino shear suppression corroborated by WGCU.
warehouse_value: FEMA HURRICANE LALA (EM-3652-HI, 2026-08-25) and TROPICAL STORM NOLO (EM-3654-HI, 2026-09-25)
